doc.title: David Friesen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2024

title: Musicians who do not listen
summary: Friesen says some technically amazing players do not listen, which he cannot use, yet he avoids judging.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I like it a lot. And when you’re playing with someone who too often has bad manners I think that person is removed from your phone list, at least in my experience.

Yeah I mean when that happens that means the person is too full of self, is too involved in himself or herself you know. And my attitude about that is this: it might work for someone else, it doesn’t work for me, but — and I have played with — mention no names or whether they’re famous or not — I have played with some people that are amazing. I mean technique is just outasight and everything, but they don’t listen at all, to what’s happening. So that’s something I can’t play with or use in the music that I play. But you know everyone has a way they want to do things. I try to stay clear of any judgments or anything. And also putting people down. I mean like I’m not even putting that person down that doesn’t listen, who won’t work with what I do. But the way I see it, Monk, is that everyone is trying to do their best. We’re all human. You know? We’re all trying to I think do our best and to play music we all want to be appreciated. So whatever I can do to help that, you know, I try to do. You know I’ve been asked what do you think of this player and that player. And most times these players that I’m mentioning have been incredible players you know it’s just amazing you know.
